subject: English Home Language

source.subtopic: Uses different sentence types (statements, questions, commands) and full punctuation

show.line: Three kinds of sentence. A statement tells. A question asks. A command gives an order. Sit down!

rounds.prompt: Close the door. What kind of sentence is this?
rounds.praise: Yes! It tells someone what to do.

rounds.prompt: The sky is blue. What kind of sentence is this?
rounds.praise: Yes! A statement tells us something.

rounds.prompt: Give the dog a command. Tell it to sit. Say it.
Statement, question or command? Sort the sentences.
Read this command out loud, like a teacher.
Which mark usually ends a command?
rounds.praise: Yes! A full stop, or an exclamation mark if it is loud.

hints: Telling? Statement. Asking? Question. Ordering? Command.
A command often starts with a doing word. Sit. Open. Wash.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! Wash your hands. I will say what kind it is.
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Wash your hands tells you what to do. It is a command.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's think together. Is it asking? No. It is telling you to do something. A command!

parent_line: Can tell statements, questions and commands apart.
